mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority and national civil registry of the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada acceded to the Apostille Convention on 11 January 2024) or consular legalization for non-Hague member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not required for domestic filing; Hague Apostille by the Québec Ministry of Justice if the certificate must be used abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized UBO Declaration and Consent to Act as Director / Canadian Resident Director exemption declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in Quebec or competent notarial authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for foreign-origin instruments; specimen signatures notarized before a Quebec notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police Clearance Certificate / Criminal Record Certificate for each responsible officer and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal records authority or national police authority of the person's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization through the competent embassy/consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming source of funds and business purpose for SWIFT/wire capital injection
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated financial institution maintaining the founder's corporate or personal banking relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank seal and officer signature verified by notary; Hague Apostille if expressly required by the Quebec receiving institution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all directors, officers, shareholders and 25%+ UBOs against FINTRAC politically exposed domestic/foreign person indicators, Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act, OFAC SDN list, UK consolidated sanctions, and UN Security Council consolidated lists. ISIC 7490 trade remedy defense consulting is rated Low_Risk_Standard, but any PEP match, OFAC link, or UN designation triggers enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth verification and senior management approval before any Swift_Wire or Wire_Transfer instruction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Registre des entreprises (REQ) online portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) requires a French-language corporate name or a French version that appears at least as prominently as any version in another language; a transliterated version of the foreign trade-defense firm name may be used only in Roman/Latin script; only Arabic numerals, Latin-script letters and permitted symbols are accepted; corporate designators must be French (e.g., 'Inc.', 'Corp.' accepted as in common use) and the name must be distinct from every existing enterprise name in the REQ database; generic French descriptors such as 'Conseils', 'Services', 'Études' are recommended for clarity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registraire des entreprises refuses a name, the applicant or authorized mandatary may submit a written demande de révision (internal review) to the Directeur de la révision within 15 days of the refusal notice, stating the corrected name or the legal arguments supporting distinctiveness. If the internal review is denied, an appeal may be filed before the Court of Québec (chambre civile) within 30 days of notification. As a practical alternative, the applicant may immediately file a new name reservation with a different distinctive component at no procedural penalty.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partial – A mail-forwarding or administrative virtual office is accepted as the correspondence address, but the corporation must maintain a real physical registered office (siège social) in Quebec where the minute book, registers and records are kept; the registered office must be identifiable and accessible to the Registraire des entreprises and Revenu Québec. For ISIC 7490 anti-dumping trade defense consulting, a virtual office alone is insufficient to satisfy bank KYC requirements for opening a corporate account receiving Swift_Wire and Wire_Transfer payments; a lease or sub-lease of physical premises or a valid registered-office-service arrangement with a licensed Quebec firm is required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 30% quantified risk of a desk audit or unannounced on-site inspection by FINTRAC (client identification files), Registraire des entreprises (registered office production demands) or Revenu Québec (GST/QST and corporate books) within the first 24 months of registration; probability increases to approximately 55% if the corporation receives cross-border wire transfers without a corresponding physical office record.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c. S-31.1, as amended, especially ss. 16-26, 106-118, 120-121, 214; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 7-14, 34-35; optional federal route under the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 6-9, 19, 106, 114-121.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Enterprise Registration and Legal Publicity Division, operated through the Espace Entrepreneurs online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de constitution (Articles of Incorporation) filed electronically with REQ; issuance of the Certificate of Constitution and the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA or CBCA; shares may be issued with or without par value for consideration determined by directors; no escrow account is required for a general business corporation. Non-resident ownership is permitted unless expressly restricted in the Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as the First Board of Directors, that: (1) the initial subscription for 1,000 common shares at CAD 1.00 per share is accepted, and share certificates shall be issued upon full payment; (2) the registered office is established at the address stated in the Articles, in the Province of Quebec, where the statutory records and minute books shall be kept; (3) [Name] is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, and [Name] is appointed Secretary-Treasurer, each with authority to execute banking, wire-transfer and trade-remedy engagement documents; (4) the corporate seal and bank account resolutions are approved; and (5) officers are authorized to complete all filings and pay applicable fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Name Search Module in Espace Entrepreneurs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search in the REQ central enterprise registry. Verify that the proposed name is distinctive, lawful, and compliant with the Charter of the French Language. Reserve the name through REQ for 90 days, ensuring it contains a mandatory legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', or 'Ltée'. Record the reservation receipt number for use in the Articles.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name in French or bilingual form
REQ name search and reservation receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for lack of distinctiveness, submit a materially different name, or obtain a written consent from the holder of a confusingly similar name, then reapply through REQ.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel and all incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts de constitution under the Business Corporations Act (Québec). Include the corporate name, registered office address, share structure, restrictions, number of directors, and the names of first directors. Ensure each incorporator signs the Articles; electronic signatures are accepted. Verify that the activity description covers ISIC 7490 trade-remedy defense consulting and that no reserved legal act is described unless separately authorized.
required_dossiers: Identification and residency declarations of incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ raises a pre-filing validation query, revise the defective provision, obtain fresh signatures where necessary, and resubmit the corrected Articles within 15 days of the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing, Fee Payment, and Issuance of Certificate of Constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Espace Entrepreneurs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into REQ Espace Entrepreneurs using the authenticated profile. Select the incorporation application for a societe par actions. Upload the finalized Articles, complete the mandatory legal publicity information, and pay the applicable filing fee. REQ examines the file and issues the Certificate of Constitution plus the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). Download both documents and retain them in the minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of default or a query, provide the missing declarations or corrected address information within 30 days. If the certificate is still refused, amend the Articles through a supplementary application and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution on Share Subscription, Registered Office, and Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors — internal corporate act, no government filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution, approve the initial share subscription, establish the registered office at the Articles’ address, approve the corporate seal, and direct the opening of the corporate minute book with registers of directors, shareholders, and officers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the minutes contain discrepancies with the Articles, adopt a corrective board resolution and, where the registered office changes, file the updated address with REQ.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Officers and Establishment of Banking Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, together with the chosen Canadian chartered bank or credit union
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pass a board resolution appointing the President/Chief Executive Officer and Secretary-Treasurer. Open a Canadian corporate bank account with SWIFT wire and wire-transfer capabilities. Provide the bank with the board resolution, Certificate of Constitution, NEQ, and beneficial ownership declarations required under FINTRAC Anti-Money Laundering rules.
required_dossiers: Bank signatory cards and KYC/beneficial ownership forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank’s compliance team requests further ownership detail, supply an organizational chart and attestation of ultimate beneficial owners; resubmit the banking package within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Declaration and Legal Publicity Update with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after the constitution, file the initial enterprise declaration with REQ listing the registered office, directors, officers, principal activity code ISIC 7490, and contact information. Maintain the declaration by filing amendments whenever directors, address, or activities change.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is filed late, pay the late fee and file the complete declaration promptly; REQ will update the register once the default is cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Trade Remedy Representation and Professional Title Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian International Trade Tribunal (CITT) and, if legal services are provided, the Barreau du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Review whether the corporation will provide only trade-remedy defense consulting or will engage in acts reserved to licensed lawyers. For consulting only, no CITT-specific representative license is required, but all marketing materials must avoid implying legal practice. If services include legal representation, retain or employ lawyers licensed by the Barreau du Québec and register representation credentials with the relevant tribunal docket office.
required_dossiers: Barreau du Québec license attestation (for individual legal counsel)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tribunal or law society objects to the corporate scope, restrict services to consulting, remove legal representation language, and arrange for a licensed lawyer to act as independent counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Office Occupancy, Fire Safety, and Occupational Health and Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal building inspection department; Quebec fire safety service; Commission des normes, de l'equite, de la sante et de la securite du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a municipal occupancy permit for the registered office confirming compliance with the Quebec Construction Code and structural load limits. Arrange a local fire safety inspection and correct any deficiencies. Register the workplace with CNESST and implement the mandatory first-aid and hazard prevention program for an office-based consulting activity.
required_dossiers: Lease or proof of ownership of the registered office
CNESST employer registration and hazard prevention records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If deficiencies are identified, carry out the required fire, structural, or occupational health corrections and request a reinspection within 10 business days; seek a temporary occupancy certificate for non-public back-office functions if immediate risks are low.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) — Licensing and Registration Directorate for the statutory enterprise registration; for any future industrial facility, Ministere de l'Economie, de l'Innovation et de l'Energie (MEIE).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Enterprise Registration Certificate (Certificat d'immatriculation) issued under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1; where reserved legal services are provided, the individual lawyer's permit issued by the Barreau du Quebec.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III — Exempt from full environmental impact assessment for an administrative office engaged in trade-remedy defense consulting; a certificate of authorization or attestation from MELCCFP would become mandatory only if the corporation later develops a physical industrial project or waste-handling facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Current office-based operations generate no process wastewater or industrial air emissions and therefore have no applicable discharge thresholds. If a future industrial operation is added, process effluent must meet the standards of the Quebec Clean Water Regulation and municipal sewer by-laws, including pH 6.0 to 9.5, total suspended solids not exceeding 15 mg/L, 5-day BOD not exceeding 20 mg/L, and oil and grease not exceeding 10 mg/L; volatile organic compound emissions must comply with the Clean Air Regulation, and any residual hazardous waste must be managed under the Quebec Residual Materials Regulation with appropriate manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the municipal fire safety service confirming compliance with the Quebec Fire Safety Code, including evacuation plans and portable extinguishers; municipal occupancy certificate and structural load inspection confirming the office floor live-load limits under the Quebec Construction Code; workplace clearance through CNESST registration, hazard identification, and first-aid equipment compliance for a standard office consulting environment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for corporate income tax, GST/HST, and customs-related tax administration; Quebec: Revenu Québec for Quebec corporate income tax and QST. Portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Revenu Québec Mon dossier entreprise (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated federal/provincial business corporation: (1) file articles of incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Quebec Business Corporations Act; (2) obtain the CRA Business Number (BN) automatically upon incorporation through Corporations Canada or by filing the Initial Return with CRA; (3) establish CRA program accounts for corporate income tax (RC0001), GST/HST (RT0001), payroll (RP0001), and import/export (RM0001) using Form RC1 or online via Represent a Client; (4) register with Revenu Québec for QST and provincial remittance accounts using the corresponding Revenu Québec registration form or the CRA/Revenu Québec coordinated one-step registration. Foreign entities not yet incorporated in Canada may register for a non-resident business number and program accounts by filing Form RC1 and may be required to provide a Canadian representative for service of process.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - a Canadian business corporation is a separate tax resident entity taxed in Canada on worldwide income when it is resident in Canada under common law or deemed resident under the Income Tax Act; no pass-through classification is available; Quebec provincial income tax is imposed on taxable income allocable to Quebec, and non-resident shareholders are not subject to deemed Canadian tax classification merely by reason of shareholding.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists in Canadian tax law. A Canadian corporation cannot elect pass-through status; entity classification is determined by the Income Tax Act and corporate law. Relevant elections for cross-border structures include the capital dividend election under subsection 83(2) of the Income Tax Act and the section 216 election for non-residents earning Canadian rental income. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act apply statutorily without an elective regime and may deny deductions or require inclusion for payments subject to hybrid mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/QST - Goods and Services Tax under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec Sales Tax under the Quebec Taxation Act, administered co-operatively by CRA and Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in any calendar quarter or in the immediately preceding four calendar quarters; same threshold applies for GST/HST registration and Quebec QST registration for persons carrying on business in Quebec, subject to special exemptions for taxi, ride-sharing, and other regulated sectors.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC) system. There is no mandatory digital stamping of invoices. Electronic invoicing is permitted and must be supported by an audit trail under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec Taxation Act. E-filing of GST/HST returns is mandatory for most registrants and Revenu Québec requires electronic remittance and filing of QST returns for businesses above prescribed thresholds; export transactions must be transmitted electronically to the CBSA where an export declaration or eManifest is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for exported goods applies when the supplier exports tangible personal property as part of the supply, export occurs within specified timelines (generally within 60 days after delivery or, if consideration is due before delivery, within 60 days after the due date), and the supplier retains documentary proof of export. Services supplied to a non-resident person, including international trade-remedy legal advisory and anti-dumping defense consulting, are zero-rated if provided to a non-resident and not acquired for use exclusively in Canada. The exporter must maintain contemporaneous evidence that the goods left Canada or the service was performed outside Canada, that payment is from a non-resident source, and that title and risk passed outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank credit/foreign exchange receipt evidence
Commercial Invoice and signed contract for the export supply
Customs broker or freight forwarder export records demonstrating physical movement of goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec will deny zero-rating if export documentation is incomplete, inconsistent, or fails to evidence physical export or non-resident service recipient. Reassessment can claw back uncollected GST and QST plus interest; civil penalties may include the gross negligence penalty under the Excise Tax Act equal to a substantial percentage of understated tax, and Quebec may impose analogous provincial penalties. Retrospective audit periods may be extended beyond the normal reassessment period in cases of misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims can lead to criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting as the central monetary and financial-system stability authority; the Department of Finance Canada administers the Exchange Fund Account and all exchange-rate policy matters; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) prudentially regulates all federally chartered Schedule I and Schedule II banks; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and supervises all reporting entities; under the Retail Payment Activities Act (S.C. 2021, c. 24), the Bank of Canada also registers and supervises retail payment service providers. Canada maintains no separate foreign-exchange administration bureau and issues no exchange-control permits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both capital and current account. Canada imposes no exchange controls, no prior-approval regime, no profit-remittance license, and no restriction on dividend, royalty, or service-fee flows to non-resident shareholders under the Currency Act, the Financial Administration Act, or the Bank of Canada Act. Dividends paid by a Quebec business corporation to a non-resident shareholder are subject to Part XIII withholding tax at a 25% statutory rate, generally reduced to 5% for a U.S. corporate shareholder under the Canada-United States Tax Convention and to 5-15% under other tax treaties. Professional consulting fees in the ISIC 7490 trade-remedy defense scope constitute treaty-protected business profits absent a Canadian permanent establishment, and no exchange-control hurdle impedes retainer invoicing in CAD, USD, EUR, or any other freely convertible currency. The principal compliance burdens are documentary: FINTRAC reporting for any wire transfer at or above CAD 10,000, sanctions screening under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, beneficial-ownership disclosure at account onboarding, and Form T1135 reporting for foreign investment property exceeding CAD 100,000. The CAD floats freely; no convertibility restriction, profit-blockade mechanism, or capital-repatriation quota exists for this corporate profile.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandated conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline for service revenue, export receipts, or any other foreign-currency earnings. A Canadian exporter or consulting firm may lawfully retain 100% of foreign-currency proceeds in domestic or offshore foreign-currency accounts. For Income Tax Act purposes, foreign-currency revenue must be translated into CAD under the functional-currency rules of section 261 or at the Bank of Canada published exchange rate; unrealized and realized foreign-exchange gains or losses are taxable or deductible under section 39. Foreign affiliates and foreign investment property exceeding CAD 100,000 aggregate cost must be reported annually on Form T1135. No approval from the Bank of Canada or the Department of Finance is required for conversion, disposal, or transfer of export or consulting receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
Desjardins Group (Groupe Desjardins, Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for primary treasury concentration, escrow custody, or capital-injection routing, because foreign fintech platforms that are not licensed Canadian banks may not take demand deposits or extend credit and expose the corporation to uninsured counterparty and regulatory risk. MEDIUM for ancillary, low-value disbursement clearing after funds have first settled through a domestic Schedule I bank. Any non-bank payment provider operating in Canada must be registered as a retail payment service provider with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act and, if engaged in money services, registered as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC; in Quebec, money-services businesses must also hold registration with the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). Offshore digital EMIs lacking Canadian registration cannot lawfully provide payment processing to this entity on a recurring basis, and their use must be supported by a written PSP/MSB registration certificate, sanctions-screening evidence, and a documented third-party provider risk assessment.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under FINTRAC customer due diligence rules, corporate account opening requires verification of the identity of every director, signing officer, and beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the corporation. In practice, Schedule I banks operating in Quebec require at least one director or duly appointed authorized signatory to attend an in-person interview at a Canadian branch for the initial account opening, particularly when non-resident ownership is present. Fully remote video-KYC opening is available at RBC, TD, BMO, and National Bank for low-risk professional-services corporations, provided all principals hold valid government-issued identification (Canadian passport, driver's licence, or a recognized foreign travel document) and the corporate resolution designating signatories is authenticated. For non-resident directors without Canadian identification, a physical visit, a notarized or apostilled identity package, and bank-reference letters are mandatory. The Registraire des entreprises du Québec attestation (NEQ certificate), the federal corporate registry extract, and a board resolution confirming the trade-remedy defense business profile must accompany the application regardless of channel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial-ownership chain involving offshore holding jurisdictions (e.g., British Virgin Islands, Cayman Islands, Panama) or layered multi-jurisdiction ownership with no clear economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registraire des entreprises du Québec attestation; complete corporate organizational chart tracing every intermediary entity to the ultimate natural-person beneficial owners; registered-agent certificate of incumbency for each offshore entity; notarized passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds letters; three years of audited or reviewed financial statements; and a board resolution identifying the commercial rationale for the holding structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment patterns in which a non-Canadian manufacturer or foreign party to an anti-dumping proceeding pays the Canadian consulting corporation's legal fees on behalf of another defendant or client.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed retainer and engagement letter; official case documentation from the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) and the Canadian International Trade Tribunal (CITT) evidencing the proceeding; detailed invoices describing professional services rendered; written third-party payer authorization with beneficial-ownership disclosure of the payor; sanctions, PEP, and terrorism-financing screening results for all parties; and an undertaking to provide underlying contracts and time records on demand.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a registered-office or virtual-office address as the sole corporate location, with no substantive operating presence in Quebec or Canada.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease or sub-lease agreement; Quebec NEQ registration certificate; corporate registry extract; GST/QST and payroll account registrations; utility bills; proof of office insurance; staffing or service-provider agreements; and a business plan demonstrating operational substance in the trade-remedy consulting practice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-velocity cross-border wire traffic or average account balances materially inconsistent with the stated consulting revenue profile of ISIC 7490.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed 12-month cash-flow forecast; client list with counterparty jurisdictions; written AML/ATF risk assessment and compliance program; compliance officer designation; sample engagement contracts; and a standing undertaking to supply invoices, settlement statements, and case records for every wire upon request.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red flags associated with personal accounts used for corporate transactions, commingling of client funds, or non-resident directors with unusual transaction counterparties in politically exposed or sanctioned regions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate banking mandate form and board resolution designating sole corporate bank accounts; clean separation of personal and corporate banking; accounting-system controls and monthly reconciliations; identification and background documentation for every signatory; declaration of non-PEP status or PEP disclosure where relevant; and FINTRAC-compliant large-transaction record-keeping protocols.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions from non-resident shareholders are routed by SWIFT MT103 (or Fedwire from the United States) to the corporation's operating account at a Schedule I bank in Canada. Field 50K must name the remitting shareholder; Field 59 must carry the exact legal name of the Quebec business corporation, its Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), and the 12-digit Canadian account number formatted as institution-transit-account, together with the beneficiary bank's SWIFT/BIC code. The payment description should state 'SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION - [Corporation Name] - shareholders' resolution dated [YYYY-MM-DD]' to preserve a complete audit trail. No Bank of Canada approval or exchange-control filing is required, but any transfer at or above CAD 10,000 triggers a FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Report by the receiving bank. The corporation must update the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, record the share issuance in its minute book, file the annual return reflecting share capital, and retain the subscription agreements and non-resident investor declarations. Operating retainers received from foreign clients enter under the narrative 'PROFESSIONAL SERVICES / TRADE REMEDY CONSULTING'; no conversion mandate applies, and CAD, USD, or EUR balances may be settled at prevailing market rates through authorized Canadian banks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound international disbursements for expert fees, foreign-counsel retainers, co-defendant cost sharing, and settlement payments are cleared through the SWIFT MT103 rail. Domestic Canadian-dollar payments above CAD 25,000 settle in real time over the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS), while smaller CAD payments clear through the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS). For goods-based settlements connected to anti-dumping mandates, a documentary letter of credit issued under ICC UCP 600 by the Canadian corporation's bank is the appropriate instrument, with CAD or USD drafts, a full set of clean onboard bills of lading, commercial invoices, certificates of origin, and any requisite CBSA or CITT duty or security documents. USD disbursements are debited from a domestic USD clearing account and settled via Fedwire or CHIPS through a U.S. correspondent bank. Cross-border CAD payments to U.S. beneficiaries clear through the Canadian Direct Clearing and Settlement System or SWIFT correspondent arrangements. Every outgoing wire at or above CAD 10,000 is reported to FINTRAC, and each payment must pass OFAC, United Nations, and Special Economic Measures Act sanctions screening before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts for immediate conversion between CAD, USD, EUR, and GBP
Vanilla deliverable FX forwards with tenors up to 24 months for CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/GBP exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or restricted emerging-market currencies arising from foreign counterparties in anti-dumping proceedings
FX swaps for short-term liquidity rotation between CAD and USD clearing accounts
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for long-duration receivables or capital-structure hedging
European-style plain-vanilla OTC FX options (puts and calls) transacted with Schedule I bank counterparties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each fiscal year-end; no extension available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of approximately CAD 3.31 per day up to CAD 189.20; continued default may lead to administrative suspension, revocation of registration, and legal incapacity of the enterprise

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporate Annual Return under Canada Business Corporations Act (if the company is incorporated federally and registered in Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 60 days of the corporation's anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may result in dissolution by Corporations Canada; late-filing penalties and reinstatement fees apply

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Quebec business corporation must appoint an auditor unless all shareholders, pursuant to a unanimous shareholder agreement or unanimous consent, waive the audit requirement for that fiscal year; public companies and distributing corporations are subject to compulsory independent audit under Canadian securities law
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises and for most Canadian publicly listed entities; private enterprises may elect Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or IFRS under Part I or II of the CPA Canada Handbook

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Quebec Annual Declaration must identify registrable persons (individuals with 25% or more control, or de jure / de facto control). Every share transfer affecting these positions must be recorded in the securities register; the company must maintain and update the register of registrable persons and file any relevant changes within 30 days of receipt of notice

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
